questions.question: For a sequence $(a_n)_{n = 1}^{\infty}$, what is the $N$-th partial sum?
When is $\sum_{n = 1}^{\infty}a_n$ called convergent?
options: When all terms $a_n$ are equal, so the partial sums grow at a fixed rate
When the partial sums $(S_N)_{N = 1}^{\infty}$ converge to some $L\in\mathbb{R}$

questions.question: Which choice of $a_n$ shows that $\sum a_n$ can diverge while $\sum\dfrac{a_n+a_{n+1}}2$ converges?
Suppose $\sum_{n=1}^\infty a_n$ converges. Which series must also converge?
Suppose $\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}a_n$ diverges. Which statement is true? A different choice of $(a_n)$ may be used for each constructed series below; all sums run from $n=1$ to $\infty$.
options: Each of $\sum(a_n+a_{n+1})/2$, $\sum(-1)^na_n$ and $\sum a_na_{n+1}$ can converge.
The series $\sum(-1)^na_n$ must diverge for every such choice of $(a_n)$.
The series $\sum(a_n+a_{n+1})/2$ must diverge for every such choice of $(a_n)$.
The series $\sum a_na_{n+1}$ must diverge for every such choice of $(a_n)$.

questions.question: Which condition is necessary for $\sum_{n = 1}^{\infty}a_n$ to converge?
options: The partial sums are all zero

questions.question: If the partial sums $(S_N)_{N = 1}^{\infty}$ converge to $L\in\mathbb{R}$, which statement is correct?
options: $S_N$ is not related to the series

questions.question: If the sequence of partial sums $(S_N)_{N = 1}^{\infty}$ diverges, what is true of $\sum_{n = 1}^{\infty}a_n$?
options: The terms must all be zero

questions.question: Which statement captures the limitation of the condition $a_n\to 0$?
options: It guarantees convergence, since the terms eventually become negligible
It implies every partial sum is zero
It is necessary for convergence but does not guarantee convergence

questions.question: Which object receives the name 'sum of the infinite series'?
options: The real limit $L$ of the partial sums

questions.question: The harmonic series shows which boundary point about the condition $a_n\to 0$?
options: Terms tending to zero make partial sums constant
A divergent series cannot have terms tending to zero
Terms tending to zero do not by themselves ensure convergence
A series with positive terms cannot diverge

questions.question: Suppose $S_N = \sum_{n = 1}^{N}a_n$ and $(S_N)$ has no real limit. Which conclusion follows?
What sequence decides whether $\sum_{n=1}^\infty a_n$ converges?
What does $S_N$ add in an infinite series?
options: All infinitely many terms at once

questions.question: What does it mean for an infinite series to diverge?
options: The first term is not defined
Its sequence of partial sums diverges
The partial sums are always zero

questions.question: If $S_N=1-\frac{1}{N}$, what is $\sum_{n=1}^\infty a_n$?
If $a_n=1$ for all $n$, what are the partial sums $S_N$?
If $a_n=0$ for all $n$, what is $\sum_{n=1}^\infty a_n$?
Why is $a_n\to0$ only a necessary condition for convergence?
options: Some series with terms tending to $0$ still diverge
It guarantees convergence of every series
It is unrelated to partial sums
It means all partial sums equal $0$

questions.question: Suppose $a_n$ does not tend to $0$. What can be concluded about $\sum_{n=1}^\infty a_n$?
